---
title: "First Look at a Geospatial File: What to Check Before You Trust It"
date: 2026-09-05
categories: [tool, geometry, bilingual]
description: "Upload a GeoJSON or a Shapefile and get an instant summary — feature count, geometry type, CRS, bounds, attributes, invalid/empty/duplicate geometries — in Python and R on the same map."
---

Before you validate, fix, or check topology, it helps to know what
you're actually holding. A feature count in the thousands changes what
checks are even practical. A CRS you didn't expect explains a map that
looks wrong before you've touched a single geometry. A handful of
exact duplicates might be an import artifact, not a data-quality
problem worth chasing.

This isn't a repair tool and it isn't a topology report — it's the
five-second first look that tells you which of those tools you
actually need next.

Just want the summary, without the rest of the reading? Use the
[standalone tool](/tools/geospatial-file-inspector.html) — same
engine, less prose.

## 1. Upload your file

A `.geojson`, or a shapefile: either as a single `.zip`, or as the
individual `.shp`/`.dbf`/`.shx` files (and optionally `.prj`) selected
together.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mutable uploadedFiles = null
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// A native <input type="file"> (WebGeoDS.Upload.createControl(), see
// shared/upload.js) — see its doc comment there for why, over an
// Observable Inputs `viewof`-bound widget.
uploadControl = WebGeoDS.Upload.createControl({
  label: "Upload",
  onChange: (files) => { mutable uploadedFiles = files; }
})
```

${uploadControl}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mutable uploadStatus = WebGeoDS.Upload.defaultStatus
```

${uploadStatus}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
{
  const result = await WebGeoDS.Upload.load(uploadedFiles);
  mutable uploadStatus = result.message;
}
```

## 2. Why start with a summary?

Eight numbers, each answering a question you'd otherwise have to dig
for:

- **Features** — how many rows. Determines whether an O(n²) check
  (like the [Topology Checker's](topology-errors.qmd) pairwise
  overlap/gap detection) is even practical to run.
- **Geometry type** — Point, Line, Polygon, or a mix. Some checks only
  apply to one family; a "mixed" result is itself useful information.
- **CRS** — the coordinate reference system the file claims to be in.
  Not verified against the actual coordinates here — that mismatch
  detection is a distinct, more involved check, covered in
  [Coordinate Reference Systems](crs-mismatch.qmd) and the
  [standalone CRS Inspector](/tools/crs-inspector.html).
- **Bounds** — the bounding box, in the file's own CRS units. A
  bounding box in the thousands or millions instead of the -180..180 /
  -90..90 range is usually the first hint of a CRS problem, before any
  dedicated check runs.
- **Attributes** — how many non-geometry columns, and their names. How
  much there is to a feature beyond its shape.
- **Invalid** — geometries that fail the Simple Features validity
  rules. See [Geometry validity](geometry-validity.qmd) for what that
  actually means and how to fix it.
- **Empty** — geometries with no coordinates at all. Easy to miss in a
  raw file, and something naive code (yours or a library's) can choke
  on silently.
- **Duplicates** — exact repeats (identical coordinates), detected by
  comparing binary geometry representations, not a full topological
  equality check. Fast enough for a large file; the
  [Topology Checker](topology-errors.qmd) has the slower, more
  thorough version if you need it.

## 3. Shared map and summary

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
sharedMap = {
  const map = new window.WebGeoDS.Map({ center: [12.5, 41.9], zoom: 4, height: "480px" });
  await map.ready();
  return map;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
sharedMapEl = sharedMap.element
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Same coloring convention as geometry-validity.qmd's VALIDITY_PAINT
// — green valid, red invalid.
INSPECT_PAINT = ({
  "fill-color": [
    "case",
    ["==", ["get", "valid"], true],
    "#2ea44f",
    "#e05252"
  ],
  "fill-opacity": 0.55
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// The summary cards' own state, separate from reading pyInspect/
// rInspect directly: those are the CodeCells' cached values, which
// Reset below has no way to clear (there's nothing to re-run) —
// without this, clicking Reset would empty the map but leave both
// summary cards showing stale numbers. Set alongside each map update
// below, cleared alongside the map reset further down.
mutable pySummary = null
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mutable rSummary = null
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
pyInspect = WebGeoDS.getCellValue("inspect-py", Generators)
{
  if (pyInspect) {
    // mapFeatures (WGS84), falling back to features: the default
    // inspect-py code returns both, but the CRS-mismatch example in
    // section 6 deliberately returns only "features", still in Web
    // Mercator — that's the whole point of that example (see its own
    // callout below), so it must NOT be silently reprojected here.
    const mapData = pyInspect.mapFeatures ?? pyInspect.features;
    await sharedMap.setGeoJSON("inspect-py", mapData, { paint: INSPECT_PAINT });
    // Zooms to whatever was just inspected — same as the standalone
    // tool. Without this the CRS-mismatch example in section 6 would
    // load fine but stay invisible: the map would just sit at its
    // fixed initial view over Italy instead of jumping to wherever the
    // Web Mercator coordinates actually land, missing the whole point
    // of that example.
    await sharedMap.fitToData(mapData);
    mutable pySummary = pyInspect.summary;
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
rInspect = WebGeoDS.getCellValue("inspect-r", Generators)
{
  if (rInspect) {
    // Same mapFeatures/features fallback as pyInspect above.
    const mapData = rInspect.mapFeatures ?? rInspect.features;
    await sharedMap.setGeoJSON("inspect-r", mapData, { paint: INSPECT_PAINT });
    await sharedMap.fitToData(mapData);
    mutable rSummary = rInspect.summary;
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Two summary cards side by side — Python's and R's — instead of one
// merged card: unlike a FeatureCollection (where combining both
// languages' results on one map is the whole point of a shared map),
// merging two "total feature count" numbers wouldn't mean anything.
// Seeing them agree (or notice where they don't, e.g. a differently
// formatted CRS string between GDAL bindings) is itself the point.
statCard = (label, s) => {
  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  wrap.style.flex = "1";
  wrap.style.minWidth = "260px";

  const heading = document.createElement("div");
  heading.className = "webgeods-label";
  heading.textContent = label;
  wrap.appendChild(heading);

  const box = document.createElement("div");
  box.className = "webgeods-stat-grid";
  wrap.appendChild(box);

  const row = (rowLabel, value) => {
    const dt = document.createElement("div");
    dt.className = "webgeods-stat-label";
    dt.textContent = rowLabel;
    const dd = document.createElement("div");
    dd.className = "webgeods-stat-value";
    dd.textContent = value;
    box.append(dt, dd);
  };

  if (!s || s.total === 0) {
    row("Features", "0");
    return wrap;
  }

  const geometryLabel = s.geometryTypes.length > 1
    ? `Mixed (${s.geometryTypes.join(", ")})`
    : (s.geometryTypes[0] ?? "—");

  row("Features", s.total.toLocaleString());
  row("Geometry", geometryLabel);
  row("CRS", s.crsWarning ? `${s.crs} ⚠️ ${s.crsWarning}` : (s.crs ?? "Unknown"));
  row("Bounds", s.bounds ? s.bounds.join(", ") : "—");
  row("Attributes", `${s.attributeNames.length}${s.attributeNames.length > 0 ? ` (${s.attributeNames.join(", ")})` : ""}`);
  row("Invalid", String(s.invalid));
  row("Empty", String(s.empty));
  row("Duplicates", String(s.duplicates));

  return wrap;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
statCardsRow = {
  const row = document.createElement("div");
  row.style.display = "flex";
  row.style.flexWrap = "wrap";
  row.style.gap = "16px";
  row.append(statCard("Python", pySummary), statCard("R", rSummary));
  return row;
}
```

${statCardsRow}

```{ojs}
resetInspection = async () => {
  for (const id of ["inspect-py", "inspect-r"]) {
    if (sharedMap.getGeoJSON(id)) {
      await sharedMap.setGeoJSON(id, { type: "FeatureCollection", features: [] });
    }

}
```

```{ojs}

resetMapButton = {
```

## 4. Inspect: summarize your file

Run the same summary in Python or R on the current data (your file
uploaded above, or the example already loaded below).

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Python

```{.webgeods-python #inspect-py}
#| package: geopandas, shapely
import geopandas as gpd
from shapely.geometry import shape

gdf = None
for path in ["/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip"]:
    try:
        gdf = gpd.read_file(path)
        break
    except Exception:
        pass

if gdf is None:
    a = {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[12.40, 41.80], [12.50, 41.80], [12.50, 41.90], [12.40, 41.90], [12.40, 41.80]]]}
    c = {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[12.75, 41.80], [12.85, 41.90], [12.75, 41.90], [12.85, 41.80], [12.75, 41.80]]]}
    gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
        {"name": ["square", "square (copy)", "bowtie"], "population": [1200, 1200, None]},
        geometry=[shape(a), shape(a), shape(c)],
        crs="EPSG:4326"
    )

# CRS is reported in the file's OWN units below (see section 2/6) — a
# bounding box in the hundreds of thousands is itself the "something's
# off" signal, which reprojecting here would erase. Only a MISSING CRS
# gets corrected (assumed WGS84, flagged) — there's nothing native to
# report otherwise.
crs_warning = None
if gdf.crs is None:
    gdf = gdf.set_crs("EPSG:4326")
    crs_warning = "No CRS found in the file — assuming WGS84 (EPSG:4326)."

if "name" not in gdf.columns:
    gdf["name"] = [f"geometry {i+1}" for i in range(len(gdf))]

# Three per-feature checks, each cheap and vectorized (no O(n²)
# pairwise comparisons — unlike the Topology Checker's check_gap()/
# check_overlap(), this is a fast first look, not an authoritative
# topology report).
gdf["valid"] = gdf.geometry.apply(lambda g: g is not None and g.is_valid)
gdf["empty"] = gdf.geometry.apply(lambda g: g is None or g.is_empty)
# Exact-match only (same WKB bytes) — catches a copy-pasted row, not a
# topologically-identical polygon traced with different vertex order.
gdf["duplicate"] = gdf.geometry.to_wkb().duplicated()

for col in gdf.columns:
    if col != "geometry":
        gdf[col] = gdf[col].fillna("")

attribute_columns = [c for c in gdf.columns if c not in ("geometry", "valid", "empty", "duplicate")]
geometry_types = sorted(set(gdf.geometry.geom_type))
bounds = [round(float(b), 6) for b in gdf.total_bounds]
crs = gdf.crs.to_string() if gdf.crs is not None else None

# MapLibre/GeoJSON require WGS84 — the summary above intentionally
# stays in the file's own native CRS (see comment above), so the map
# gets its own throwaway reprojected copy instead of reusing gdf
# directly. gdf.crs is never None here (a missing CRS was already
# assumed WGS84 above).
map_gdf = gdf if gdf.crs == "EPSG:4326" else gdf.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

{
    "features": gdf.__geo_interface__,
    "mapFeatures": map_gdf.__geo_interface__,
    "summary": {
        "total": len(gdf),
        "geometryTypes": geometry_types,
        "crs": crs,
        "crsWarning": crs_warning,
        "bounds": bounds,
        "attributeNames": attribute_columns,
        "invalid": int((~gdf["valid"]).sum()),
        "empty": int(gdf["empty"].sum()),
        "duplicates": int(gdf["duplicate"].sum())
    }
}
```

## R

```{.webgeods-r #inspect-r}
#| package: sf, geojsonsf, jsonlite
data <- NULL
for (path in c("/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip")) {
  data <- tryCatch(sf::st_read(path, quiet = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(data)) break
}

if (is.null(data)) {
  wkt_a <- "POLYGON((12.40 41.80, 12.50 41.80, 12.50 41.90, 12.40 41.90, 12.40 41.80))"
  wkt_c <- "POLYGON((12.75 41.80, 12.85 41.90, 12.75 41.90, 12.85 41.80, 12.75 41.80))"
  geoms <- sf::st_as_sfc(c(wkt_a, wkt_a, wkt_c), crs = 4326)
  data <- sf::st_sf(name = c("square", "square (copy)", "bowtie"), population = c(1200, 1200, NA), geometry = geoms)
}

# CRS is reported in the file's OWN units below (see section 2/6) — a
# bounding box in the hundreds of thousands is itself the "something's
# off" signal, which reprojecting here would erase. Only a MISSING CRS
# gets corrected (assumed WGS84, flagged) — there's nothing native to
# report otherwise.
crs_warning <- NULL
if (is.na(sf::st_crs(data))) {
  sf::st_crs(data) <- 4326
  crs_warning <- "No CRS found in the file — assuming WGS84 (EPSG:4326)."
}

if (!("name" %in% names(data))) {
  data$name <- paste("geometry", seq_len(nrow(data)))
}

data$valid <- sf::st_is_valid(data)
data$empty <- sf::st_is_empty(data)
# Exact-match only, via WKT text comparison (st_as_binary() also
# exists but WKT is the more commonly relied-on round-trip in sf) —
# same reasoning as the Python side: not a topological check.
data$duplicate <- duplicated(sf::st_as_text(sf::st_geometry(data)))

attribute_names <- setdiff(names(data), c("geometry", "valid", "empty", "duplicate"))
geometry_types <- sort(unique(as.character(sf::st_geometry_type(data))))
bnd <- sf::st_bbox(data)
crs_input <- sf::st_crs(data)$input

# MapLibre/GeoJSON require WGS84 — the summary above intentionally
# stays in the file's own native CRS (see comment above), so the map
# gets its own throwaway reprojected copy instead of reusing `data`
# directly. st_crs(data) is never NA here (a missing CRS was already
# assumed WGS84 above).
map_data <- if (isTRUE(sf::st_crs(data) == sf::st_crs(4326))) data else sf::st_transform(data, 4326)

# jsonlite::unbox() marks a value as a genuine scalar, explicitly,
# field by field — the alternative would be toJSON(auto_unbox = TRUE)
# globally, but that unboxes EVERY length-1 vector in the structure,
# not just the fields meant to be scalars: geometryTypes is length 1
# for the overwhelmingly common case of a single-geometry-type file,
# and auto_unbox would silently turn ["POLYGON"] into bare "POLYGON",
# breaking .join() on the JS side (verified empirically via Playwright
# — a real TypeError, not a hypothetical one). unbox()'d here instead
# of relying on a blanket flag, so geometryTypes/bounds/attributeNames
# stay real arrays (jsonlite's default for a vector) with no special
# handling needed for them at all.
result <- list(
  features = jsonlite::fromJSON(geojsonsf::sf_geojson(data), simplifyVector = FALSE),
  mapFeatures = jsonlite::fromJSON(geojsonsf::sf_geojson(map_data), simplifyVector = FALSE),
  summary = list(
    total = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(data)),
    geometryTypes = geometry_types,
    crs = if (is.null(crs_input)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(crs_input),
    crsWarning = if (is.null(crs_warning)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(crs_warning),
    bounds = unname(round(as.numeric(bnd), 6)),
    attributeNames = attribute_names,
    invalid = jsonlite::unbox(sum(!data$valid)),
    empty = jsonlite::unbox(sum(data$empty)),
    duplicates = jsonlite::unbox(sum(data$duplicate))
  )
)

# Round-tripped through JSON once more, whole-object this time: R's
# atomic vectors (geometry_types, bounds, attribute_names) don't cross
# the webR->JS bridge as plain JS arrays on their own the way a
# jsonlite-parsed list does — same reasoning already applied to
# "features" above, just for the summary fields too.
jsonlite::fromJSON(jsonlite::toJSON(result, null = "null"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
```

:::

## 5. Same spatial question, two languages

Python and R read the same numbers off the same engines, but the
accessors differ:

**Python** (GeoPandas)

```python
len(gdf)                  # feature count
gdf.geometry.geom_type    # per-feature geometry type
gdf.crs.to_string()       # CRS
gdf.total_bounds          # [minx, miny, maxx, maxy]
gdf.geometry.to_wkb()     # exact-match key for duplicate detection
```

**R** (sf)

```r
nrow(data)                        # feature count
sf::st_geometry_type(data)        # per-feature geometry type
sf::st_crs(data)$input            # CRS
sf::st_bbox(data)                 # xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax
sf::st_as_text(sf::st_geometry(data))  # exact-match key
```

The CRS string is the one place they can genuinely disagree in
formatting, not just vocabulary.[^inspect-crs-format]

[^inspect-crs-format]: `st_crs()$input` returns whatever string the
file's own CRS definition resolved to (often `"EPSG:4326"` for a clean
case, but sometimes a full WKT string for a less common one), while
GeoPandas' `.crs.to_string()` goes through PyPROJ's own formatting —
same underlying CRS, not always the same displayed text. Worth knowing
before assuming a mismatch between the two summary cards above means
an actual data problem.

## 6. Load an example

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
loadExampleButton = (label, pyCode, rCode) => {
  const button = document.createElement("button");
  button.textContent = label;
  button.onclick = async () => {
    await Promise.all([
      window.WebGeoDS.CodeCell.find("inspect-py")?.setCode(pyCode),
      window.WebGeoDS.CodeCell.find("inspect-r")?.setCode(rCode)
    ]);
    document.getElementById("inspect-py")?.scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth", block: "center" });
  };
  return button;
}
```

The reusable cell pair above already loads a small dataset with one
exact duplicate and one invalid geometry whenever nothing has been
uploaded — click **▶ Run** on both languages above to see it. This
button swaps in a dataset with a deliberately unusual CRS instead, to
see the bounds stat do its job.[^crs-mismatch-bounds]

[^crs-mismatch-bounds]: Web Mercator coordinates plotted at the same
zoom level as geographic coordinates land far outside any sensible map
view — that's the "bounds in the hundreds of thousands" tell in
practice, not just in the abstract. Detecting exactly this kind of
mismatch, and converting a file to a different CRS, is what
[Coordinate Reference Systems](crs-mismatch.qmd) and its [standalone
tool](/tools/crs-inspector.html) do.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
pyCrsExampleCode = `import geopandas as gpd
from shapely.geometry import shape

# The same square as the default example, but reprojected to Web
# Mercator (EPSG:3857) — coordinates in the hundreds of thousands to
# millions instead of -180..180, exactly the tell described in
# section 2 above.
gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    {"name": ["square"]},
    geometry=[shape({"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[12.40, 41.80], [12.50, 41.80], [12.50, 41.90], [12.40, 41.90], [12.40, 41.80]]]})],
    crs="EPSG:4326"
).to_crs("EPSG:3857")

if "name" not in gdf.columns:
    gdf["name"] = [f"geometry {i+1}" for i in range(len(gdf))]

gdf["valid"] = gdf.geometry.apply(lambda g: g is not None and g.is_valid)
gdf["empty"] = gdf.geometry.apply(lambda g: g is None or g.is_empty)
gdf["duplicate"] = gdf.geometry.to_wkb().duplicated()

for col in gdf.columns:
    if col != "geometry":
        gdf[col] = gdf[col].fillna("")

attribute_columns = [c for c in gdf.columns if c not in ("geometry", "valid", "empty", "duplicate")]
geometry_types = sorted(set(gdf.geometry.geom_type))
bounds = [round(float(b), 6) for b in gdf.total_bounds]
crs = gdf.crs.to_string() if gdf.crs is not None else None

{
    "features": gdf.__geo_interface__,
    "summary": {
        "total": len(gdf), "geometryTypes": geometry_types, "crs": crs, "bounds": bounds,
        "attributeNames": attribute_columns,
        "invalid": int((~gdf["valid"]).sum()), "empty": int(gdf["empty"].sum()), "duplicates": int(gdf["duplicate"].sum())
    }
}`
rCrsExampleCode = `wkt <- "POLYGON((12.40 41.80, 12.50 41.80, 12.50 41.90, 12.40 41.90, 12.40 41.80))"
data <- sf::st_sf(name = "square", geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(wkt, crs = 4326))
data <- sf::st_transform(data, 3857)

data$valid <- sf::st_is_valid(data)
data$empty <- sf::st_is_empty(data)
data$duplicate <- duplicated(sf::st_as_text(sf::st_geometry(data)))

attribute_names <- setdiff(names(data), c("geometry", "valid", "empty", "duplicate"))
geometry_types <- sort(unique(as.character(sf::st_geometry_type(data))))
bnd <- sf::st_bbox(data)

result <- list(
  features = jsonlite::fromJSON(geojsonsf::sf_geojson(data), simplifyVector = FALSE),
  summary = list(
    total = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(data)), geometryTypes = geometry_types,
    crs = jsonlite::unbox(sf::st_crs(data)$input),
    bounds = unname(round(as.numeric(bnd), 6)), attributeNames = attribute_names,
    invalid = jsonlite::unbox(sum(!data$valid)), empty = jsonlite::unbox(sum(data$empty)),
    duplicates = jsonlite::unbox(sum(data$duplicate))
  )
)
jsonlite::fromJSON(jsonlite::toJSON(result, null = "null"), simplifyVector = FALSE)`
```

```{ojs}

```

## 7. Where to next

A summary is a starting point, not an endpoint:

- **CRS looks off?** → [Coordinate Reference Systems](crs-mismatch.qmd)
  covers the mismatch heuristic above in depth, with conversion — or
  use the [standalone CRS Inspector](/tools/crs-inspector.html)
  directly.
- **Invalid geometries?** → [Geometry validity](geometry-validity.qmd)
  explains why, and how `make_valid()`/`st_make_valid()` fix it — or
  use the [standalone Validator](/tools/geojson-shapefile-validator.html)
  directly.
- **Everything valid, but the dataset still looks wrong?** →
  [Topology errors](topology-errors.qmd) covers overlaps, gaps,
  slivers, duplicates, and dangles — relationships *between* features,
  not properties of any one of them — or use the
  [standalone Topology Checker](/tools/topology-checker.html).
- **Just needed the numbers?** The
  [standalone Inspector](/tools/geospatial-file-inspector.html) has
  the same summary, no reading required.
